children.text: 10,000 GitHub Stars: Thank You for Believing in Privacy-First AI
Meetily just crossed 10,000 GitHub stars. A heartfelt thank you to the community that made this possible, and a look at what we're building next.

children.alt: Meetily celebrates 10,000 GitHub stars - open source meeting transcription milestone

children.text: This post celebrates the 10,000 GitHub stars milestone reached in February 2026. Numbers below reflect that milestone moment. Meetily has since grown to 31,000+ stars, 599,000+ downloads, and 3,300+ forks. See /open-source for current stats.

Meetily just hit 10,000 GitHub stars! We started this journey as an internal tool because we needed a meeting assistant that kept our client conversations truly private - on their own infrastructure, under their control. We weren't comfortable with cloud-based solutions processing sensitive discussions on external servers.
Today, 88,000+ people have downloaded Meetily, 920+ developers have forked it, and it supports 99+ languages across the globe. This incredible support from the community means everything to us.
Our mission has always been simple: bring AI to you, not your data to us. Thank you for believing in privacy-first meeting intelligence. Here's what's next.
We didn't set out to build a popular open source project.

We built Meetily because we needed a meeting assistant that didn't upload our conversations to someone else's servers. Open sourcing it was our way of giving back to the community that's given us so much - and we hoped others might feel the same way about data privacy.
Turns out, a lot of people feel the same way.
Today, Meetily crossed 10,000 GitHub stars. The response from the community has been overwhelming, and we're incredibly grateful.
Let's take a moment to appreciate what this community has built together:
10,000+ GitHub stars - from developers, teams, and privacy advocates worldwide
88,000+ downloads - people who tried Meetily and chose privacy
920+ forks - developers building on top of Meetily
Each of those numbers represents a real person who decided their meeting data should stay on their own device.
To the early adopters who filed issues when the app crashed (and it crashed a lot in those early days) - thank you.
To the contributors who submitted pull requests, fixed bugs, and improved documentation - thank you.
To the users who told their colleagues about Meetily because they believed in the mission - thank you.
To the developers who forked the repo and built something new on top of it - thank you.
To the teams who chose Meetily over polished cloud alternatives because privacy mattered more than convenience - thank you.
To everyone who starred the repo - even if you haven't tried it yet - thank you. Every star tells us we're building something worth building.
If you ever need help, have feedback, or just want to say hi - reach out to us at meetily@zackriya.com. We read every email.
The journey from zero to 10K wasn't a straight line.
Version 0.0.1 was macOS-only, required CMake and Python, and needed a separate backend server running alongside the app. Our own team complained about it.

Today, Meetily is a single-click installer for Windows and macOS. Transcription runs locally with Whisper or Parakeet models. You choose your AI provider for summaries - local models or your own API keys. Everything lives in a local SQLite database on your device.
The core promise never changed: your meetings stay yours.
Hitting 10K stars doesn't mean we're done. It means more people are counting on us to keep going.
Speaker diarization - Know who said what. We have a proof of concept ready and it's one of our most requested features.
File import - Drop in an audio file and get a transcript. Simple, but useful for podcasters, researchers, and journalists.
Better local summarization - Cloud models still produce better summaries than local ones. We're working to close that gap so privacy doesn't mean compromising on quality.
More integrations - Calendar sync, custom templates, and better export options based on what you've been asking for.
We let our users guide the product. Every feature is built based on real feedback from people actually using Meetily.
Every week, another AI product launches with "privacy" somewhere in its marketing. Most of them still upload your data to their cloud.
We took a different approach. Meetily exists because we believe:
Your meeting recordings should never leave your device
You should choose which AI processes your data
Open source is the only way to prove "privacy-first" actually means something
Good software doesn't require giving up your data
10,000 stars tells us this matters to you too.
If you've read this far but haven't tried Meetily yet, here's your sign. Download it, try it with your next meeting, and see what privacy-first actually feels like.
And if you're already a user - share it with someone who needs it. The best growth we've ever had is word of mouth from people who genuinely like the product.
Privacy-first meeting transcription. 10,000 developers can't be wrong.

children.alt: Under the EU AI Act, a meeting tool's risk depends on how you use it: summarizing calls is not high-risk, scoring employees is high-risk from December 2027, reading emotions at work is banned since February 2025, and EN 18286 is the first standard

children.text: Your Meeting Tool's Risk Level Under the EU AI Act Isn't Set by the Vendor. It's Set by You.
The EU AI Act's four risk categories cover uses, not products. The same meeting tool can be low-risk, high-risk or banned. Plus the 2027 timeline and EN 18286.
